title: Laravel-Lang Packagist tag rewrite and Composer autoload backdoor campaign
summary: Source-backed emergency advisory for a Composer/Packagist compromise pattern involving historical Git tag rewrites, Packagist source reference anomalies, Composer autoload.files backdoor loading, PHP payload retrieval, and credential harvesting behavior.

safe_versions: Reinstall from a verified clean source reference after upstream tag provenance is confirmed.

detection_rationale: Packagist metadata and prior source snapshots can show historical versions repointed to new source/dist references without executing package code.
GitHub tag snapshots can show rewritten tags, high-volume tag activity, fork-origin targets, or unreachable commits across related repositories.

Composer artifacts can be statically inspected for autoload.files entries such as src/helpers.php and PHP credential-stealer behavior including payload retrieval, disabled TLS verification, cloud metadata reads, Kubernetes token reads, /proc environ reads, and developer credential file discovery.
remediation: Block affected Packagist versions in Composer policy, artifact proxies, and CI lockfile review until source refs are verified clean.
Audit composer.lock for laravel-lang/lang, laravel-lang/http-statuses, laravel-lang/attributes, and laravel-lang/actions, including source and dist references.
Remove vendor copies containing suspicious autoload.files helpers and rebuild vendor directories from verified clean lockfiles.
Hunt for listed domains, temp staging paths, DebugChromium.exe, cloud metadata access, Kubernetes token reads, /proc environ access, and PHP/VBS background execution.
Rotate Composer, GitHub, SSH, cloud, Vault, Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, and application credentials if an affected artifact was installed or autoloaded.
